title: US, China and Russia could be in a new UFO arms race as fears grow over who will reveal alien secrets first: report
excerpt: The United States could face a new geopolitical challenge from China and Russia over who reveals significant information about unidentified flying objects
content:
The United States could face a new geopolitical challenge from China and Russia over who reveals significant information about unidentified flying objects (UFOs) first.

US Representative Eric Burlison has warned that Washington risks handing its rivals a propaganda victory if the Trump administration fails to deliver on its promises of greater transparency about UFOs and possible extraterrestrial life, according to the New York Post.

Burlison believes that if China or Russia releases credible information before the United States, it could damage America’s reputation for openness.

In February 2026, President Donald Trump directed federal agencies to identify and release government records concerning unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs), UFOs and potential evidence of extraterrestrial life.

The Pentagon has since published several batches of historical records, videos and intelligence reports. However, questions remain about how much information authorities can disclose without compromising national security.

Russia and China reportedly preparing UFO disclosure

Amid the growing interest in UFO disclosure, science filmmaker and UFO researcher Simon Holland has made a separate, extraordinary claim involving Russia and China.

In a September 23 interview with the Daily Express, Holland alleged that researchers linked to the two countries had received communications from an extraterrestrial civilization.

Holland claimed that an unnamed source connected to radio astronomy research had informed him about the supposed discovery. He further alleged that Russia had shared advanced quantum messaging technology with China, potentially allowing both countries to communicate with extraterrestrial intelligence.

According to Holland, the countries could be waiting for a politically advantageous moment to announce their findings.

He suggested that such an announcement could embarrass the Trump administration by raising questions about what American intelligence agencies have disclosed to the public.

However, these claims remain unverified. Neither Russian nor Chinese authorities have publicly confirmed receiving an extraterrestrial signal. No independently authenticated message or scientific data supporting Holland’s account has been made available.

Russia and China have previously collaborated on quantum communications research. In one reported experiment, scientists established a secure quantum communication link spanning approximately 3,800 kilometers.

However, that experiment concerned encrypted communications between locations on Earth, not extraterrestrial contact.

Declassified UFO files raise new questions

The debate comes as Washington continues releasing previously classified records concerning unexplained aerial sightings.

The Pentagon’s third batch of UAP documents, released on June 12, 2026, included historical intelligence reports describing unusual incidents both inside and outside the United States.

Among the documents was a CIA intelligence report concerning an unidentified object spotted above Harare International Airport in Zimbabwe in July 2008.

According to the report, observers described a disc-shaped object with rotating lights that changed colors before it rapidly ascended out of sight. The account also mentioned beams reportedly emanating from the object.

Those familiar with the incident reportedly debated whether the object could have been an advanced foreign reconnaissance device or something of extraterrestrial origin.

However, the CIA document was marked as intelligence that had not been finally evaluated. It did not establish the object’s origin or independently verify its reported capabilities.

A potential race for technological supremacy

Beyond the political implications of UFO disclosure, some researchers and former intelligence officials have raised concerns about a possible competition to understand technology allegedly recovered from unidentified craft.

Jordan Flowers, executive director of the UAP Disclosure Foundation, has suggested that China and Russia may have recovered unidentified objects and attempted to reverse-engineer them.

Speaking to NewsNation in June, Flowers argued that the possibility of foreign governments studying such technology raised serious national security questions.

However, his remarks were based on allegations rather than publicly verified evidence that either country possesses extraterrestrial spacecraft.

The broader discussion also comes amid growing military competition in space.

In September 2026, US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink publicly acknowledged that the United States had deployed weapons in orbit capable of supporting military space-control operations.

The announcement drew attention to escalating tensions involving American, Chinese and Russian space capabilities. However, no evidence links those deployed weapons to recovered UFO technology.

For now, the debate over UFO disclosure remains largely a question of government transparency, unresolved sightings and competing claims about classified information.

Although some incidents remain unexplained, publicly available evidence has not established that China, Russia or the United States possesses technology of extraterrestrial origin.
